content.value: This section provides an overview of the core system architecture, outlining its major subsystems, service communication models, and the deployment strategy used to ensure scalability and reliability.

The system follows a microservices-based architecture. Each module is independently deployable and communicates via REST and gRPC channels. The architecture ensures that components remain loosely coupled yet highly cohesive.
The training dataset consists of 1.2M DNA sequences, each annotated with cellular expression levels. The dataset highlights gene–protein interactions crucial for biomarker prediction.

A custom Perceiver-based architecture was implemented. The model was trained on TPUs for 60 epochs using mixed-precision training. Key optimizations included aggressive gradient checkpointing and batched sequence encoding.
The model achieved significant improvements over baseline methods. Results show robust generalization across multiple protein-level prediction benchmarks.
Plans include scaling the model depth, integrating transformers-based locality attention, and deploying the model into a stream-optimized data pipeline.
